interest: Reveals U.S. wartime planning on Micronesia and improvised civilian sources of Japanese geographic intelligence.
overview: State Department decimal file 894.014 (File 1476) spans January 1940 through December 1944 and documents U.S. diplomatic, legal, and military-intelligence efforts concerning Japanese territorial claims, mandated territories, boundaries, and cartographic intelligence during World War II. The collection focuses heavily on high-level strategic planning and inter-agency coordination involving the Department of State, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the War and Navy Departments regarding the legal status, wartime administration, and postwar disposition of the Japanese Mandated Islands in Micronesia and offshore claims such as Shinnan Gunto (Spratly Islands) and Marcus Island. Simultaneously, the file reflects wartime operational intelligence gathering, capturing how intercepted commercial atlases, seized propaganda maps, and unsolicited donations of prewar travel guides, industrial blueprints, and terrain photographs from private citizens, corporations, and diplomatic posts were evaluated, routed, and incorporated into military intelligence libraries to support the Pacific war effort.
